Damage Modifiers Table (SR2 p.112). The Injury Modifier is a universal target-number modifier applying to nearly every Success Test the injured character attempts — except tests to resist or avoid damage. The Initiative Modifier is applied to Reaction before Initiative dice are rolled; if it drops Reaction to 0 or less, the character cannot act that Combat Turn.

Damage LevelInjury ModifierInitiative Modifier
Uninjurednonenone
Light+1−1
Moderate+2−2
Serious+3−3
Deadlyunconscious or near death

How the levels stack

Within a single column the levels are not cumulative — only the highest level reached counts. Across the two columns they are cumulative.

Worked example from the book: a character Moderately wounded in Stun and Lightly wounded in Physical takes +2/−2 for the Stun and +1/−1 for the Physical, for a total of +3 target number and −3 Initiative.

Condition Monitor

Two tracks, Stun and Physical, each marked at Light / Moderate / Serious / Deadly. Boxes fill at 1 / 3 / 6 / 10. Physical damage beyond Deadly runs into Physical Damage Overflow.

Recovering damage (SR2 p.112–113). Stun and Physical heal differently and at different rates.

Stun

Roll Body or Willpower, whichever is higher, against a base Target Number 2. That target number is modified by any injury modifiers the character currently has, Stun or Physical.

Recovering one box has a base time of 60 minutes; the actual time is the base divided by the successes rolled. After that time one box is erased.

  • The character must be resting completely. Interrupt the rest and the recovery aborts — re-roll using the condition at that moment, but the result can never be better than the first roll.
  • A character knocked unconscious by Deadly Stun does not wake until their Stun is reduced to Serious.
  • Rest is the only way to recover Stun. No medical treatment helps, and no known spell does either. A Stim Patch buys time at a long-term cost (p.250).

Curative magic

The treat and heal spells (p.155) each mend a number of boxes equal to the successes rolled. Treat must be applied within one hour of the injury; heal has no time limit. A character can be magically treated or healed only once per set of injuries.
